notes: PB5084 owns the fix (open: the 1985 Segmentation module is accepted-inert at --std 85, and its rule list carries the three §1985:XVI.1.4.3 rows, not this one). §1985:VI.6.7.4 GR1 has two sentences. The first, "Execution of the ALTER statement modifies the GO TO statement in the paragraph named procedure-name-1 so that subsequent executions of the modified GO TO statement cause transfer of control to procedure-name-2", is implemented: AlterEnsureScan gives every paragraph an ALTER names one per-program-instance field (EmitFields initializes it to the written GO TO target, or to no target for the 1985 target-less GO TO), AlterGoTo and AlterBindBareGoTo bind the GO TO of such a paragraph as a transfer to the field's current value (EmitGoTo), and BindAlter resolves both procedure-names and EmitAlter assigns procedure-name-2's entry to the field, so the most recent ALTER governs; ALTER itself is refused from 2002 (COBOL0810). Probed at --std 85: a GO TO performed before any ALTER goes to its written target; ALTER with and without PROCEED retargets it; two entries in one ALTER each take effect; an ALTER inside IF and one written after the GO TO it names take effect; a section as procedure-name-2 transfers to its first paragraph; a qualified procedure-name-2 (TZ OF S3) is the one reached where another section has a TZ; a target-less GO TO goes where its ALTER sent it, and a second ALTER of the same paragraph replaces the first. The second sentence is NOT implemented: "Modified GO TO statements in independent segments may, under some circumstances, be returned to their initial states (see page XVI-2, Independent Segments)". VisitSectionDefinition reads a section's segment-number only for the 2002 removal gate (its summary: "Parsed and ignored at 85"), no binder or emitter member reads it, and the field EmitAlter assigns is never reset on a transfer into a section of segment-number 50 through 99, so the modified GO TO stays modified where §1985:XVI.1.4.3 puts the segment back in its initial state. docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.18 records that as a deliberate leniency; no owner decision closes it. The witness is the first sentence only: one ALTER of an unsegmented paragraph, displaying A then B.

next.reason: 1985: "Execution of the ALTER statement modifies the GO TO statement in the paragraph named procedure-name-1"; 2023: "No ALTER clause; GO TO GR1 just says: control is transferred to procedure-name-1". No 2023 clause holds the ALTER statement. The 2023 GO TO rules give a fixed target and no way to modify it, so ALTER and its effect on GO TO are dropped.
